title: Analysis of Auditory Steady-State Responses in Rats
author: Pavel Prado
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.wejfbcn
materials: Acoustic stimuli can be generated using standard hardware/software. In our experiments, continuous tones of 8 kHz sinusoidally-modulated in amplitude (95% depth) at 115 Hz are generated using the ASSR software module of the AUDIX system (Havana, Cuba). Stimulus intensity is fixed at 50 dB SPL.

steps.title: Anesthetize rat
steps.instruction: Inject ketamine at 75.0 mg/kg intraperitoneally and diazepam at 5.0 mg/kg intraperitoneally.

steps.title: Maintain anesthesia and temperature
steps.instruction: Give supplemental doses of ketamine/diazepam as needed to keep the animal in an areflexic state; keep body temperature at 37.0 ± 0.1 °C using a temperature‑control system.

steps.title: Administer atropine
steps.instruction: Inject atropine sulfate at 0.06 mg/kg intramuscularly to reduce mucosal secretions.

steps.title: Fit custom ear molds and earphone
steps.instruction: Insert custom‑fitted ear molds (replacing the original foam) into the rat’s ear and couple an ER 3A Etymotic Research insert earphone for monaural acoustic stimulation.

steps.title: Calibrate acoustic stimulation system
steps.instruction: Reference acoustic levels to a Brüel & Kjær artificial ear (type 4152) and calibrate with a Brüel & Kjær 2250 sound‑level meter using a Brüel & Kjær 4144 microphone.

steps.title: Place differential recording electrodes
steps.instruction: Insert stainless‑steel needle electrodes subdermally: vertex (positive), neck (negative), and thorax (reference).

steps.title: Amplify, filter, and digitize signals
steps.instruction: Amplify recordings with a gain of 1.2 × 10⁴, band‑pass filter between 10 Hz and 300 Hz, then digitize at 16‑bit resolution sampling at 920 Hz.

steps.title: Acquire artifact‑free epochs and recordings
steps.instruction: Reject online any segment with peaks >50 mV; continue acquisition until 60 artifact‑free epochs of 4.45 s (4096 points) are collected per recording. Record 30 such recordings per animal, spacing consecutive recordings by 10 minutes.

steps.title: Terminate experiment and recover animal
steps.instruction: No sacrifice is required; after the recordings allow the rat to recover from anesthesia and return it to the colony.

steps.title: Organize data matrix and optional weighting
steps.instruction: Using in‑house MATLAB code, rearrange the 60 epochs from each of the 30 recordings into a matrix of 30 rows × 60 columns per animal. Optionally weight each voltage sample by dividing by the variance of its epoch, then normalize the weights by their average across all epochs before averaging.

steps.title: Average epochs and compute FFT
steps.instruction: Column‑wise average the matrix (i.e., average across the 30 recordings for each epoch). Compute the fast Fourier transform on each averaged epoch using an FFT length of 4096 points (matching the 4.45 s epoch). With a 920 Hz sampling rate the frequency resolution is 0.22 Hz; no windowing is applied.

steps.title: Determine ASSR amplitude and residual noise
steps.instruction: Define ASSR amplitude as the spectral amplitude at 115 Hz (stimulus modulation frequency). Calculate the residual noise level (RNL) by vector‑averaging the 30 spectral components on each side of 115 Hz.

steps.title: Plot time course and calculate adaptation index
steps.instruction: Plot ASSR amplitude versus time; fit a negative exponential (require r² > 0.85 and p < 0.05). If adaptation is detected, compute the adaptation index: P_adapt = 100 × (Amp_max – Amp_adapt)/Amp_max, where Amp_max is the fitted curve’s maximum and Amp_adapt is the asymptotic value (estimated at three times the exponential time constant).

steps.title: Perform statistical comparisons
steps.instruction: Compare ASSR amplitudes with the corresponding RNL using Hotelling’s T² multivariate test (AUDIX system) after averaging. Additionally, apply one‑way ANOVA (p < 0.05) and Tukey post‑hoc tests (p < 0.05) to assess stability of ASSR amplitude and RNL across epochs.
